actor_messages.text:
Learner B5, welcome to Sprint 4. Here is your official brief for the final sprint of the project.

Task Context
Sprint 4 covers the GTM Plan, Launch Checklist, A/B Experiment, Metrics Dashboard, and Final Demo Day. Your objective is to prepare the product for go-live by building the rollout strategy, designing an experiment, establishing operational launch guardrails, and synthesizing your full product journey into the final presentation.

What You Must Build
1. GTM Plan: Define target segment, core messaging, launch channels, rollout phases (beta to staged to full), and communication timeline.
2. Launch Checklist: Minimum 10 actionable items across pre-launch, launch day, and post-launch phases, each with role owners, statuses, and defined rollback/pause triggers.
3. A/B Experiment Design: Focus on your riskiest assumption using the hypothesis format ('If change X, then metric Y moves Z because W'), linked to your Sprint 2 Metric Tree, including control, variant, minimum sample size, duration, and pre-mortem.
4. Metrics Dashboard Mockup: Track at least 5 key metrics from Sprint 2, complete with metric definitions, tracking cadence, ownership, and action triggers.
5. Final Demo Day Deck: Build a comprehensive presentation following the complete 6-part narrative arc: Problem, Research, Decision, Solution, Metrics, and Next Steps.

Required Deliverables
Strategy and launch documentation, launch checklist, experiment brief, dashboard mockup, and final presentation deck covering all required sections.

Assets and Links
No external task files are provided. Your deliverables must logically build directly on your Sprint 1 research, Sprint 2 strategy and metric tree, and Sprint 3 prototype artifacts.

Deadline
Thursday, August 6, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time.

Success Standards
- Full completion and submission of all 5 deliverables before the deadline.
- Direct traceability of all metrics and success criteria to the Sprint 2 Metric Tree and North Star Metric.
- Complete narrative coherence and alignment across all four sprint artifacts in the final demo story.

Support Routing & Submission Instructions
- Submit deliverables directly to your mentor before the deadline.
- For technical guidance, task how-to questions, or draft reviews, consult your mentor.
- For program, administrative, personal, or operational issues, contact the internship group admins in the team channel.

Execute this final sprint with high standards and clear accountability.

actor_messages.text:
Learner B3, you are assigned to Sprint 3: Interactive AI-feature Prototype + 1-Page PRD + User Stories & Acceptance Criteria + Sprint Board + Technical Integration Note.

Task Context:
This sprint transitions your AI capability from concept to interactive execution. You are required to build a clickable, production-quality prototype of the AI feature scoped in Sprint 1, along with developer-ready technical and operational documentation.

Required Deliverables:
1. AI-Prototype: Hi-fi, interactive, production-quality UI built with an AI prototyping tool (such as Lovable or v0) via a public shareable link. Must include real UI states (loading, empty, error, success) and cover the complete interaction flow.
2. 1-Page PRD: A single-page lean document covering all 7 required sections: Problem, Primary User, Goals, In Scope, Out of Scope, Technical/Business Constraints (explicitly detailing AI/model constraints: cost, latency, accuracy, data availability), and at least 3 Open Questions.
3. User Stories + Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 stories in "As a / I want to / So that" format based on your Sprint 1 persona. Each story must feature at least 2 acceptance criteria in "Given / When / Then" format, and at least one story per flow must document an edge case (API failure/timeout, empty state, or mobile access).
4. Sprint Board Setup: Epics, stories, tasks, and a clear sprint goal configured in your PM tool, submitted with a board screenshot and a brief walkthrough.
5. Technical Integration Note: A 1-page sketch mapping how the AI feature connects to Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, data layer, and AI/model layer (prompt design, API, or fine-tuning approach).

Assets:
No external files are provided. You will generate and submit your shareable prototype link and artifact documents.

Deadline:
Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time. The deadline stands; scope swaps and time extensions are not granted.

Success Standard:
Deliverables must meet executive standards. The prototype must be fully navigable end-to-end without external assistance, and the PRD must provide sufficient clarity for engineering execution without clarifying questions.

Support Routing & Submission Instructions:
Submit finalized deliverables directly through the mentor path prior to the deadline. Technical guidance, execution questions, and draft feedback belong with your mentor. Administrative issues go to internship coordinator Nadeen Diaa, and tool access issues should be posted in the team group for internship admins. Scope and deadline decisions remain with management.

actor_messages.text:
Learner B7, welcome to Sprint 3. Below is your official task kickoff brief for this sprint.

Task Context
This week, you transition from concept to execution by delivering a fully navigable interactive prototype and complete technical specifications for the AI capability scoped in Sprint 1. The objective is strict product scoping, end-to-end flow design, and robust edge-case planning.

What You Must Build
1. Interactive AI Prototype: A hi-fi, production-quality clickable UI built using an AI prototyping tool (e.g., Lovable or v0). Wireframes are unacceptable. Must feature a consistent design system and reflect all core UI states: loading, empty, error, and success across the complete interaction flow.
2. 1-Page PRD: A lean single-page document covering seven mandatory sections: Problem, Primary User, Goals, In Scope, Out of Scope, Technical/Business Constraints (explicitly addressing model cost, latency, accuracy, and data availability), and at least 3 Open Questions.
3. User Stories + Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 stories written in "As a / I want to / So that" format using your Sprint 1 persona. Each story requires a minimum of 2 Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. At least one story per flow must cover an edge case (API failure/timeout, missing data, mobile access).
4. Sprint Board Setup: Epics, stories, tasks, and a clear sprint goal configured in a PM tool, submitted with a screenshot and a concise walkthrough.
5. Technical Integration Note: A 1-page technical sketch detailing connections across Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, data layer, and AI/model layer (prompt design, API, or fine-tuning approach).

Required Deliverables
- Public, shareable interactive prototype link.
- 1-Page PRD document.
- User Stories and Acceptance Criteria.
- Sprint Board screenshot and walkthrough.
- 1-Page Technical Integration Note.

Assets and Links
- No starter file assets are required for this kickoff. Use your designated prototyping and PM tools.

Deadline
- Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time. I expect this by the deadline.

Success Standard
- Deliverables must be complete, fully integrated, and precise enough that a developer could build the feature without asking clarifying questions. The prototype must be navigable from start to finish by an external user without assistance.

Support Routing & Submissions
- Final deliverables, technical execution questions, and draft reviews must be directed to your assigned mentor.
- Administrative, program, or personal inquiries should be directed to the Internship Coordinator, Nadeen Diaa.
- Infrastructure, tool access, or blocking technical operational issues should be reported to the internship admins in the team channel.

Review these requirements and begin execution immediately.

feedback.mentor_reply:
Great work on Sprint 3! Your submission fully meets the bar. The interactive Lovable prototype is now public and easy to navigate end-to-end, and your 1-page PRD covers all 7 sections thoroughly—especially the AI constraints around latency and accuracy. The Given/When/Then user stories capture realistic edge cases well, and your Trello board and Technical Integration Note provide a clear architecture blueprint.

To refine this even further for production, consider adding explicit UI error/fallback states for when AI API calls timeout, and defining exact prompt parameter templates in your technical note.

You are all set for Sprint 3. Take these learnings forward into the sprint retro and final project polish!

To build a solid Launch Checklist, you'll want at least 10 actionable items split across three distinct stages, with clear ownership and safety triggers for each item.

1. **Phases & Sample Items:**

   - **Launch Day (3-4 items):** Execute production deployment, flip feature flag to 100% traffic, test core user signup flow on live environment.
   - **Post-Launch (3-4 items):** Monitor APM crash logs for 2 hours post-release, verify event tracking in analytics, conduct launch review.

2. **Required Columns for Every Single Item:**
   - **Item Description & Phase:** The specific task to be performed.
   - **Owner:** Designated role (e.g., DevOps Lead, QA Engineer, Product Manager).
   - **Status:** Current execution state (e.g., Completed, In Progress, Pending).
   - **Rollback / Pause Trigger:** Explicit condition that forces a freeze or rollback (e.g., *"Rollback if HTTP 5xx error rate exceeds 2% over 5 minutes"* or *"Pause launch if staging smoke test fails high-severity check"*).

Setting this up as a table or spreadsheet will give you a clean, review-ready artifact.

interaction_log.summary: Explained beta, staged, and full rollout strategies with practical examples for the GTM plan.

actor_messages.text: explain beta staged and full with exampels

To keep launch risk under control, you want to expand your audience in these three phases:

- **Beta Rollout:** Release to a select, invited group of early users to catch bugs and collect feedback before going public. *Example: Giving 100 power users early access to test a new analytics feature for two weeks.*
- **Staged (Phased) Rollout:** Incrementally roll out the product to growing percentages of your total user base to monitor technical stability. *Example: Turning on a feature flag for 10% of live users on Day 1, then scaling to 50% on Day 3 if crash rates stay below 1%.*
- **Full Rollout:** Open access to 100% of your audience alongside your main public marketing push. *Example: Removing feature flag restrictions and launching public announcements across email, social media, and press.*

actor_messages.text:
Learner B4, below is your complete task brief and operational expectations for Product Sprint 3.

**Task Context**
Product Sprint 3 — Interactive AI-feature Prototype + 1-Page PRD + User Stories & Acceptance Criteria + Sprint Board + Technical Integration Note
This sprint requires moving your AI capability from concept into an interactive, functional prototype alongside complete execution documentation. You are expected to deliver production-quality artifacts that fully detail both user interactions and technical implementation.

**What You Must Build**
1. Interactive AI Prototype: High-fidelity, fully designed UI built with an AI prototyping tool (such as Lovable or v0). It must cover the full core interaction flow end-to-end with real UI states (loading, empty, error, success) and be production-quality rather than wireframes.
2. 1-Page PRD: A lean, single-page PRD covering 7 required sections: Problem, Primary User, Goals, In Scope, Out of Scope, Technical/Business Constraints (explicitly addressing cost, latency, accuracy, and data availability), and at least 3 Open Questions.
3. User Stories & Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 user stories formatted as "As a / I want to / So that" using your Sprint 1 persona. Each story must contain at least 2 Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. At least one story per flow must address edge cases such as API failures/timeouts, missing data, or mobile access.
4. Sprint Board Setup: Live board setup in a PM tool with epics, stories, tasks, and a clear sprint goal, accompanied by a screenshot and short walkthrough.
5. Technical Integration Note: A 1-page sketch outlining connections to Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, data layer, and AI/model layer (prompt design, API, or fine-tuning approach).

**Required Deliverables**
- Shareable public link to the clickable Hi-Fi AI Prototype
- 1-Page PRD document
- Document containing 5–8 User Stories with Acceptance Criteria
- Sprint Board Screenshot and Walkthrough
- 1-Page Technical Integration Note

**Assets and Links**
- No external starter files are provided. Use AI prototyping platforms (e.g., Lovable or v0) and your project management tool.

**Deadline**
- Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59:59 PM Cairo time.

**Success Standard**
Deliverables must meet strict professional standards. The prototype must be publicly accessible and navigable start-to-finish by an unfamiliar user without guidance. The PRD must fit on a single page while providing exact specifications so a developer can build without asking clarifying questions. Edge cases must be explicitly captured in acceptance criteria.

**Support Routing and Final Submission**
- Final Deliverables: Submit your complete work package directly to your mentor before the deadline.
- Technical Guidance & Draft Reviews: Route all technical implementation questions, tool queries, and requests for draft feedback to your mentor.
- Program & Administrative Inquiries: Direct administrative or program questions to the internship coordinator, Nadeen Diaa.

Review these requirements carefully and begin work immediately.

feedback.summary: The submission meets the core expectations with an interactive Lovable prototype, a detailed Trello sprint board, user stories, and a technical integration note. Key improvements include formatting acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format with explicit edge cases, and ensuring the 1-page PRD thoroughly covers AI constraints and open questions.
feedback.mentor_reply:
I reviewed your Sprint 3 submission and overall your work meets the bar nicely. The Lovable interactive prototype is clickable and feels like a real product, and your Trello sprint board is well-structured with clear Kanban workflow columns and visual walkthrough panels.

To take this from good to production-ready, here are two concrete areas to polish:
1. Reformat your acceptance criteria across the user stories into standard Given/When/Then format, and flesh out the specific edge cases (such as API call failures or missing session context) rather than leaving them as brief bullet points.
2. Check your 1-page PRD to make sure all 7 sections are clearly delineated, specifically highlighting AI model constraints (latency, cost, accuracy) and adding at least 3 open questions for developers.

Take a quick pass at tuning those acceptance criteria and PRD sections to finish out Sprint 3 strong!

**Task Context**
We are moving from raw research to concrete strategy and execution scoping. You must align your solutions with the strategic goals of Sprints.ai, map the high-level technical architecture, define measurable metrics, and establish a prioritized backlog and product roadmap.

**What You Must Build and Analyze**
Map Sprints.ai’s current platform architecture at a high level before writing user stories. Next, construct an Opportunity Solution Tree connecting outcomes to specific research insights, establish a North Star Metric and metric tree, perform a RICE scoring analysis on your top 5 bets, draft a MoSCoW-based MVP Scope Document, and design a validation-focused 4-Week Product Roadmap. Finally, coordinate an Alignment Sync with your mentor to secure formal sign-off.

**Required Deliverables**
Your final submission must include the following completed items:
- **Tech Stack Mapping**: A structured high-level overview mapping delivery, data, frontend, and existing integrations.
- **Opportunity Solution Tree**: Outcomes mapped to opportunities and solution bets grounded entirely in Sprint 1 research.
- **North Star Metric + Metric Tree**: A defined NSM with 3-4 input metrics, 1-2 lagging metrics, and at least 1 guardrail metric, noting current tracking or gaps.
- **RICE-Scored Backlog**: Detailed scoring for the top 5 solution bets with explicit tradeoff rationales (2 sentences each) for each bet.
- **MVP Scope Doc**: A MoSCoW breakdown with no more than 3 "Must Haves" and explicit strategic written reasons for descoped items.
- **4-Week Product Roadmap**: Milestones tied to validation checkpoints, learning goals, and success signals rather than a feature list.

**Assets and Links**
No external templates or document links are provided. You must build these deliverables from scratch, using professional product management formats.

**Deadline**
This task must be completed by Thursday, July 23, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time. The deadline stands. Manage your time carefully to meet this target.

**Success Standard**
Deliverables must demonstrate high analytical rigor. Your opportunities must link directly to research, metrics must be highly actionable, and the roadmap must prioritize validation and learning. You will defend these scoping decisions during the Alignment Sync.

**Support Routing**
Direct technical questions, tech stack clarifications, or draft feedback to your mentor. My expectation is that the final submission is clear, structured, and aligned with these requirements.

Learner B5, you are assigned to complete Product Sprint 3: Interactive AI-feature Prototype + 1-Page PRD + User Stories & Acceptance Criteria + Sprint Board + Technical Integration Note.

Task Context:
Move from concept to an interactive, clickable product interface. You will build a prototype of the AI capability scoped in Sprint 1, write a concise 1-page PRD, establish a functional sprint board, and document the technical integration architecture. Focus on rigorous scoping and addressing critical edge cases (such as model timeouts, missing data, and mobile usage) rather than relying only on happy paths.

What You Must Build or Analyze:
1. AI Prototype: A high-fidelity UI built with an AI prototyping tool (e.g., Lovable or v0) covering the full core flow, with realistic states for loading, empty, error, and success.
2. 1-Page PRD: A single-page lean PRD covering 7 required sections: Problem, Primary User, Goals, In Scope, Out of Scope, Technical/Business Constraints (explicitly addressing model cost, latency, accuracy, and data availability), and at least 3 Open Questions.
3. User Stories & Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 stories in "As a / I want to / So that" format derived from your Sprint 1 persona, each with at least 2 Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. Include at least one edge-case story per flow.
4. Sprint Board Setup: Epics, stories, tasks, and a sprint goal configured in a PM tool, with a board screenshot and brief walkthrough.
5. Technical Integration Note: A 1-page document detailing connections to Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, data layer, and AI/model layer (prompt design, API, or fine-tuning approach).

Required Deliverables:
- AI Prototype public clickable link
- 1-Page PRD document
- 5-8 User Stories with Given/When/Then Acceptance Criteria
- Sprint Board screenshot and walkthrough
- 1-Page Technical Integration Note

Assets:
- No pre-packaged assets are provided. Build your prototype using your selected AI prototyping platform and set up your sprint board in your PM tool.

Deadline:
- Submission deadline: Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59:59 PM Cairo time.

Success Standard:
 Deliver production-ready, unambiguous outputs. The prototype must be fully navigable start-to-finish by an unguided user, the PRD must answer developer requirements on a single page, and edge cases must be fully accounted for.

Support Routing and Submission:
- Submit your completed deliverables directly through the mentor path.
- Direct technical implementation questions and draft reviews to your mentor.
- Direct program, personal, or administrative inquiries to your Internship Coordinator (Nadeen Diaa). Access issues go to group admins. Scope, priority, and deadline decisions remain strictly under my authority.

interaction_log.summary: Initial kickoff and project brief delivered to Learner B3 for Sprint 2.

actor_messages.text:
Learner B3, we are kicking off the next phase of your project. You are expected to translate your Sprint 1 research into a concrete product strategy, a prioritized backlog, and a scoped MVP.

**Task Context**
This task requires you to align your product strategy and vision with Sprints.ai's platform, applying prioritization frameworks, defining tracking metrics, and building a strategic roadmap that reflects real trade-offs rather than a simple timeline of features.

**What You Must Build or Analyze**
* **Opportunity Solution Tree**: Map a desired outcome at the top (a specific, measurable change in learner behavior, not a vague goal) to opportunities from Sprint 1 and your proposed solution bets. Every node must trace back to Sprint 1 research.
* **North Star Metric + Metric Tree**: Define a single North Star Metric representing core value. Map 3–4 input metrics, 1–2 lagging outcome metrics, and at least 1 guardrail metric. Note current measurement methods or flag tracking gaps on Sprints.ai.
* **RICE-Scored Backlog**: Score your top 5 solution bets using Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort. Provide explicit reasoning for each component and a 2-sentence trade-off rationale explaining what you gain and give up for each.
* **MVP Scope Doc**: Create a MoSCoW breakdown with no more than 3 "Must Haves." For any item in "Should Have" or below, write an explicit, strategic reason for its descoping.
* **4-Week Product Roadmap**: Detail learning goals and specific success signals for each weekly milestone, focusing on validation and learning rather than feature delivery.
* **Tech Stack Mapping**: Document a high-level overview of how Sprints.ai delivers courses, accesses learner data, tracks analytics, and integrates third-party tools. State any assumptions where information is missing.

**Required Deliverables**
Your final submission document must include:
1. Opportunity Solution Tree
2. North Star Metric + Metric Tree
3. RICE-Scored Backlog
4. MVP Scope Doc
5. 4-Week Product Roadmap
6. Tech Stack Mapping

**Assets and Links**
No external assets or template links are provided for this sprint. You are expected to construct these documents and frameworks using the details outlined in this brief and your own research from Sprint 1.

**Deadline**
The final deliverable must be submitted by Thursday, July 23, 2026, at 20:59 UTC. This is a firm deadline.

**Success Standard**
To meet the professional standard, your strategy must be traceable to Sprint 1 findings. All prioritization metrics must contain robust, written rationale rather than arbitrary numbers. The roadmap must prioritize validated learning over static feature shipment.

**Support Routing & Submission**
All technical implementation questions, draft reviews, and your final submission must be directed to your mentor. Ensure your MVP scope and roadmap are sent to your mentor 24 hours prior to your scheduled Alignment Sync on Day 5, where you will defend your scoping choices with evidence.

This sprint focuses on turning your AI feature concept from Sprint 1 into a functional, clickable UI and engineering-ready specifications. Scope ruthlessly and account for system failure states and edge cases rather than solely designing for happy paths.

WHAT YOU MUST BUILD:
1. An interactive, hi-fi prototype of your AI capability using tools like Lovable or v0, covering the end-to-end user flow.
2. A single-page Product Requirement Document (PRD).
3. 5 to 8 user stories with Given/When/Then acceptance criteria.
4. A live Sprint Board with a clear sprint goal.
5. A 1-page Technical Integration Note showing how the capability connects to the platform stack.

REQUIRED DELIVERABLES:
- Interactive AI Prototype: Hi-fi, production-quality screens (not wireframes) built using an AI prototyping tool (e.g., Lovable or v0). Must feature a consistent visual design system, cover the full core interaction flow, include real UI states (loading, empty, error, success), and be accessible via a public, shareable link that anyone can navigate unaided.
- 1-Page PRD: A lean 1-page document containing all 7 required sections: Problem, Primary User, Goals, In Scope, Out of Scope, Constraints (technical, business, and AI/model constraints covering cost, latency, accuracy, and data availability), and at least 3 Open Questions.
- User Stories & Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 stories in "As a / I want to / So that" format based on your Sprint 1 persona. Each story must have at least 2 acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format. At least one story per flow must explicitly cover edge cases (e.g., API timeout, missing context/data, mobile access).
- Sprint Board Setup: A configured PM tool board containing epics, stories, tasks, and an explicit sprint goal, accompanied by a board screenshot and brief walkthrough.
- Technical Integration Note: A 1-page architectural sketch mapping the feature to Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, data layer, and AI/model layer (prompting, API, or fine-tuning strategy).

ASSETS AND LINKS:
No external file assets are provided. You are expected to leverage AI prototyping tools such as Lovable or v0 to build the UI deliverables.

DEADLINE:
Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59:59 PM Cairo time. Deadlines are strictly enforced; I do not grant extensions on request.

SUCCESS STANDARD:
Your work must be complete, production-ready, and fully navigable. The PRD and user stories must be precise enough that an engineering team could build the feature without asking clarifying questions, and all required failure states must be documented.

SUPPORT ROUTING AND SUBMISSION:
- Final Submission: Submit your final deliverables directly to your mentor.
- Technical Guidance & Draft Reviews: Route all implementation questions, technical guidance, and draft feedback requests to your mentor.
- Technical Blockers & Access Issues: Post in the team/internship group for assistance from internship admins.
- Program & Administrative Matters: Route administrative or personal program questions to Nadeen Diaa, Internship Coordinator.
- Scope & Schedule Authority: All scope adjustments, deadline reviews, and priority decisions remain under senior management authority.

Review these expectations and begin execution immediately.

actor_messages.text:
Learner B3, here is your official brief and expectations for Product Sprint 3.

Task Context
This week, you will move your churn-reduction MVP feature from concept into an interactive, clickable product. Focus on strict scoping and account for edge cases and system failures (such as API errors, empty states, and mobile access) rather than designing only for the happy path.

Required Build & Deliverables
1. AI-Prototype: A high-fidelity, production-quality UI generated using an AI prototyping tool (such as Lovable or v0). It must cover the full core user flow with real UI states (loading, empty, error, success) and be shareable via a public, fully clickable link. Low-fidelity wireframes are not accepted.
2. 1-Page PRD: A lean, single-page document containing all 7 required sections: Problem, Primary User, Goals, In Scope, Out of Scope, Technical/Business Constraints, and at least 3 Open Questions.
3. User Stories & Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 user stories formatted as "As a / I want to / So that" based on your Sprint 1 persona. Each story requires a minimum of 2 Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and every flow must document at least one edge case.
4. Sprint Board Setup: A live board configured in a project management tool containing epics, user stories, tasks, and an explicit sprint goal, accompanied by a screenshot and short walkthrough.
5. Technical Integration Note: A 1-page sketch detailing how your feature connects to Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, and data layer.

Assets & Links
No external starter assets or templates are provided for this sprint. You will build directly from your Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 outputs.

Deadline & Submission
The submission deadline is Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time. Submit your completed package—including the public prototype link and documentation—directly to your mentor before the deadline. Technical questions and draft reviews go to your mentor.

Success Standard
Your submission must be production-grade and fully navigable end-to-end by an external stakeholder without guidance. The PRD and user stories must be clear and detailed enough that an engineering team could build the feature without asking a single clarifying question.

Support Routing
- Technical guidance, draft reviews, and final submissions: Submit directly to your mentor.
- Operational or system access issues (e.g., Zoom access, GitHub permissions): Post in the internship team group for the internship admins.
- Administrative, program, or personal matters: Contact Nadeen Diaa, Internship Coordinator.
- Scope, priorities, approvals, and deadline decisions: Managed directly by me. Extensions or scope changes will not be granted.

Review these requirements and begin execution immediately.

You are advancing from product scoping to building an interactive, clickable prototype of the AI capability designed in Sprint 1, alongside the technical and execution documentation required for development.

1. Interactive AI Prototype: A hi-fi, fully clickable, production-quality UI built with an AI prototyping tool (e.g., Lovable or v0). 3. User Stories & Acceptance Criteria: 5 to 8 user stories in "As a / I want to / So that" format written from your Sprint 1 persona. Each story requires a minimum of 2 Given/When/Then acceptance criteria. Each flow must include at least one edge-case story (API/model timeout or failure, missing context/data, mobile access).
4. Sprint Board Setup: Epics, stories, tasks, and a sprint goal configured in a PM tool, backed by a screenshot and a short walkthrough.
5. Technical Integration Note: A 1-page sketch detailing how the AI feature connects across Sprints.ai's frontend, backend, data layer, and AI/model layer (prompt design, API, or fine-tuning).

Submit your final deliverables directly to your mentor prior to the deadline. Your submission must contain:

- Technical Integration Note

No external assets or starter files are provided for this task. You are expected to build these deliverables using your Sprint 1 outputs and standard tools.

Deadline & Success Standards:
- Deadline: July 30, 2026, at 11:59:59 PM Cairo time.
- Success Standard: Full completion of all 5 deliverables meeting the defined scoping and technical criteria, executed to a standard where an engineering team could build directly from your specification without requiring clarification.

Support & Work Routing:
- Direct all technical questions, implementation guidance, and draft feedback requests to your mentor.

feedback.mentor_reply:
تسلم إيدك، الشغل على تسليمة Sprint 3 ممتاز ومستواه عالي جداً! الـ Lovable prototype بتاع الـ AI Mentor Review Console متقفل صح من ناحية الـ UI states—سواء الـ loading skeletons أو حالة الـ error لما الـ AI review يكون unavailable—وكمان الـ PRD والـ Trello board منظمين جداً وماشيين مع الـ user flows والـ technical note.
